bull_bear.body: Final dividend INR 4/share (plus INR 12 interim); Funding for future capex (INR 3,800cr+) to be mix of debt/equity; Net debt currently low at INR 895cr providing headroom, though peak debt levels not defined due to project volatility.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Raw material price volatility (7-8% increase expected Q1); Geopolitical disruptions impacting freight and supply chains; US tariff uncertainties (10% reciprocal tariff impact, refund claims filed but not received); Execution risk in scaling new On-Highway segments (TBR/PCR) against established competitors; FX realization volatility.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Resilient and cautiously optimistic; confident in long-term structural growth and product quality; transparent about near-term margin pressures from RM costs; disciplined on capital allocation but aggressive on capacity expansion for adjacency plays.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Carbon Black business now material with 70% third-party sales acting as a hedge/margin contributor; FX hedging for EUR expected to improve significantly in FY27 vs Q4 rate of INR 99; On-Highway pricing strategy is 'at par' with market leaders (no discounting), relying on quality/brand rather than price undercutting; Government EPR norms require buying recycling certificates, not necessarily using recycled content in tyres.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividend declared of "Rs. 4/- per equity share", footnoted as the "1st Interim Dividend".
- Profitability guidance: "Expect blended margins post full commercialization to be in the range of 23-25% allowing absolute EBITDA to grow significantly".
- On returns: "On enhanced revenue backed by a superior product mix and operational strengths, do not anticipate a significant decline in ROCE as full potential is achieved."
- Credit standing cited as "CRISIL Rating: AA/Positive to AA+/Stable".
- Standalone balance sheet at Mar'26 shows total equity of Rs. 10,966 cr against non-current borrowings of Rs. 888 cr and current borrowings of Rs. 3,161 cr, on a total balance sheet of Rs. 17,713 cr.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated manufacturing ecosystem with in-house carbon black and mould production, driving cost control, quality consistency, and supply reliability.
- Global distribution network with a presence in over 160 countries and long-standing OEM partnerships, ensuring market reach and demand stability.
- Strong R&D and testing capabilities, including the NATRAX facility in Indore, enabling application-specific designs and lifecycle efficiency.
- Extensive and specialized product portfolio with over 3,600 SKUs, offering superior performance and lower total cost of ownership.
- Leadership position in the global OHT segment with over 5% market share, and the only Indian manufacturer of large ASR mining tyres.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw Material Price Volatility — Exposure to commodity price fluctuations in raw material baskets can pressure operating margins, mitigated through vertical integration (in-house carbon black) and recipe optimisation.
- Demand Cyclicality Across End-Use Sectors — Global off-highway tyre demand is linked to agricultural, industrial, and mining cycles; the company relies on a resilient aftermarket replacement segment to balance OEM cyclicality.
- Foreign Exchange Fluctuations — Multi-currency revenue footprint across Europe, Americas, and India exposes the company to forex volatility, managed through hedging and centralised treasury protocols.
- Climate-Related Disruptions — Physical climate risks and water scarcity could disrupt manufacturing; mitigation includes rooftop solar, alternative feedstocks, and a strict Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) framework.
- Changes in Regulatory Landscapes — Evolving global compliance mandates (e.g., EU REACH, IATF 16949) and trade corridor policies require continuous alignment to maintain uninterrupted market access.
- Geopolitical Developments — Global operations are exposed to geopolitical tensions that can disrupt supply chains, trade flows, and market demand across key regions.
- Cybersecurity and Data Privacy — Reliance on integrated IT systems (SAP ERP) creates exposure to cyber threats and data breaches, requiring continuous reinforcement of security policies.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as holding "Global Leadership in Off-Highway Tires" and as "India's foremost exporter in the Off-Highway tire segment, with a solid presence across agriculture, construction, mining, and industrial applications".
- Breadth is framed as a moat: "development of over 3600 SKUs" and "Sales to over 160 countries through Distribution network in the Americas, Europe, India and the rest of the world".
- In mining tires the deck claims BKT is the "Only Indian manufacturer to develop All-Steel Radial technology up to 57 inches", with a full range in both Bias and Radial technologies.
- Competitive advantages are listed as SCALABLE INFRASTRUCTURE ("Sufficient land and upstream equipment in place"), STRONGER BRAND EQUITY, and an INTEGRATED CARBON BLACK PLANT.
- Brand build-out includes Ravichandran Ashwin and Ranveer Singh as brand ambassadors, an extended Cricket Australia partnership "through to the 2028-29 seasons", and a "BKT 2.0 – The New Brand Architecture" splitting identities for the tyres business (OHT + On-Highway) and the carbon business.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Customer recognition] "BKT Receives Caterpillar 'Excellence Level' Recognition for Fourth Consecutive Year" from Caterpillar's Global Supplier Excellence Recognition (SER) program for quality, delivery and customer support.
- [History] Milestones listed include the 1st plant at Aurangabad in 1987, start of off-highway tire production in 1995, the Bhuj greenfield plant in 2015, self-reliance in carbon black in 2020, Waluj capacity raised to 55,000 MTPA in 2023, advanced carbon materials capex completed in 2024, and the 2025 announcement of capex for the premium passenger car and commercial vehicle radial tire segments.
- [Basis of reporting] Every figure in the deck is flagged "All Figures on Standalone basis"; no consolidated view is presented.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Balkrishna Industries Limited (BKT) is an Indian multinational company that engineers and manufactures specialized tyres for demanding off-highway applications, including agriculture, construction, earthmoving, mining, and port operations. The company is the largest exporter in the agricultural radial segment among Indian tyre manufacturers and the only Indian producer of All Steel Radial (ASR) mining tyres. BKT is also expanding into India's On-Highway Tyre market with two-wheeler and commercial vehicle radial tyres, supported by an in-house carbon black business that ensures raw material security and quality consistency.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Off-Highway Tyres:** Agriculture (MPT, ATV, Go-kart), Turf Maintenance, Industrial, Construction, Port Operations, OTR, Earthmoving, Mining, All Steel Radial (ASR) mining tyres up to 57-inch, with 63-inch under development, Solid tyres, Rubber tracks
- **Consumer Tyres:** Two-wheeler tyres (BKT ZENOVA, BKT THYROS), Commercial Vehicle Radial tyres (BKT m.Loadxpert, BKT Milexpert RG)
- **Carbon Black:** Carbon Black, Specialty Carbon Black

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Channel inventory at normal levels; no explicit order book data provided; TBR distribution network primary layer complete (~90 distributors), dealership expansion tied to sales ramp-up.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Strategic entry into TBR, 2W, and PCR segments targeting INR 5,000cr revenue by 2030; backward integration via Carbon Black expansion (target 360k MTPA) and captive power (64MW) to enhance cost efficiency; premium positioning in VF/IF technology tyres.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Calibrated on-highway expansion aligned with structural growth in passenger and commercial vehicle segments.
- Carbon black integration to support cost efficiency, supply security, and margin resilience.
- Focus on off-highway tyres (OHT) as a high-margin cyclical buffer, supported by infrastructure, mining, and mechanisation trends.
- Premiumisation and radialisation of product mix, including large-rim radial tyres for SUVs and EV-specific low-rolling-resistance tyres.
- Geographical expansion into underserved Tier-II and Tier-III markets through deep local partnerships.
- Supply diversification beyond Southeast Asia into emerging African markets and maintaining 60–90-day raw material inventory to insulate from price volatility.
- Adoption of Industry 4.0 digital capabilities (IoT, blockchain, digital twins) to reduce supply chain disruptions and enhance productivity.
- No explicit dividend policy, buyback, debt reduction, or reinvestment philosophy stated in the provided text.
- Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) group: all manufacturing facilities recycle process effluents back into production utility lines, mitigating freshwater risks.
- Accelerated decarbonisation through robust rooftop solar power infrastructure and scaling of alternative feedstocks such as sustainable Tyre Pyrolysis Oil.
- Halved plant incident rate while sustaining a target of zero lost-time injuries; achieved zero plant incident rate during the year.
- Delivered 3.4 lakh+ training man-hours across technical, behavioural, and compliance modules; 1,200 people trained per day in shop-floor safety systems.
- CSR spend of H 44.21 Crores in FY26, exceeding the mandated amount, focused on education, healthcare, sustainability, and rural development.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: To accelerate Vision 2030, the Company has cumulatively announced a capex outlay of ₹6,800 Crore since August 2024, to be deployed through FY 2028-29. These investments are directed towards capacity expansion and infrastructure development across OHT and on-highway tyre categories, expansion of carbon black capabilities, AI-enabled automation in the on-highway business, and sustainability initiatives. The roadmap includes ongoing manufacturing expansion of 35,000 MTPA, supported by continuous debottlenecking, to enhance OHT tyre capacity to 4,25,000 MTPA and support an 8% global market share. In parallel, captive carbon black capacity is being ramped up to 3,60,000 MTPA by Q1 FY 2026-27, strengthening integrated manufacturing advantage. These investments also position the Company to scale the on-highway tyre business, with a targeted contribution of 20% to overall revenues by FY 2029-30.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Replacement market expected to be the primary growth driver, providing recurring demand and greater revenue visibility, particularly in commercial vehicle and logistics-linked segments.
- Higher vehicle ownership, utilisation, and freight movement expected to drive tyre demand across segments, with total tyre consumption projected to rise from ~2.6 million tonnes to 10.7 million tonnes by 2050.
- Continued investments in infrastructure, mining, and mechanisation expected to support demand for off-highway tyres.
- Rising tyre demand strengthens the strategic value of carbon black integration by supporting cost efficiency, supply security, and margin resilience.
- Global tyre market projected to grow 3.7% from USD 202.83 billion in 2025 to USD 210.33 billion in 2026, with long-term valuations reaching USD 249.51 billion by 2030 at a CAGR of 4.4%.
- Indian tyre market growing from USD 14.45 billion in 2025 at a 7.49% CAGR, driven by a 60% expansion of the national highway network and replacement segment commanding 58% of total demand.
- Domestic off-highway tyre market of USD 1.22 billion growing at 5.52% to reach USD 1.69 billion by 2031, led by public capex into highways, freight corridors, and mining operations.
- Sharp premiumisation wave driving product mix, with passenger cars leading at 32% share and medium-sized tyres dominating at 50%.
- Radial technology cornering over 60% market share and tubeless fitments over 70% in India.
- EV-specific low-rolling-resistance tyres projected at a rapid 12.5% CAGR, engineered for heavier battery packs with high torques.
- Tyre retreading emerging as a focus, driven by lifecycle extension, cost-efficiency, and sustainable fleet management.
- Manufacturers successfully executing calibrated, consecutive price hikes averaging 6% to 8% in domestic replacement markets and 2% to 4% internationally to insulate margins from cost-push inflation.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: BKT delivered record OHT volumes in Q4FY26 but faced margin compression from raw material spikes and FX losses, while strategically pivoting into the on-highway segment (TBR/2W/PCR) with a massive INR 2,000 crore capex approval to drive long-term adjacency growth despite near-term cost headwinds.
